reason: The text explicitly portrays the Israelites (בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) as followers of Yahweh in multiple ways: (1) they move upon the command of Yahweh ('עַל־ פִּי יְהוָה'); (2) their leader Moses appeals directly to Yahweh in prayer ('וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ יְהוָה'); (3) Moses invokes Yahweh's authority when addressing the people ('מַה־ תְּנַסּוּן אֶת־ יְהוָה'); (4) Yahweh provides for them and guides their leader's actions; and (5) they are explicitly identified as Yahweh's people whose relationship with him is central to the narrative. While the passage also depicts their rebellion and doubt (complaining about water, testing Yahweh), this does not negate their portrayal as followers but rather illustrates the tension between their covenant status and their imperfect faith.
